1      async Task<DocumentStoreUsage?> IDocumentStoreUsageSource.TryCreateUsage(CancellationToken token)
 2      {
 3          var usage = new DocumentStoreUsage(Subject, this)
 4          {
 5              Database = await Options.Tenancy.DescribeDatabasesAsync(token).ConfigureAwait(false),
 6              StoreName = Options.StoreName,
 7              DatabaseSchemaName = Options.DatabaseSchemaName,
 8              AutoCreateSchemaObjects = Options.AutoCreateSchemaObjects.ToString(),
 9              EnumStorage = Options.EnumStorage.ToString(),
10  
11              // #5543 / jasperfx#870 §5. A console building a member path into the raw JSON, or explaining why
12              // a filter on `Status` matched nothing in a document stored as `status`, cannot work it out from
13              // the JSON alone -- absence of a member and a differently-cased member look the same. The three
14              // values Casing spells (Default, CamelCase, SnakeCase) are exactly the three the contract names.
15              SerializerCasing = Serializer.Casing.ToString(),
16          };
17  
18          // Per-document-type mappings — Documents collection. Skip mappings that
19          // don't emit schema (structural-typed, internal-only) so the snapshot
20          // matches what an operator would see in the database.
21          //
22          // 9.0: BuildAllMappings forces materialization of every registered type
23          // builder into a concrete DocumentMapping. After #4303 made mapping
24          // materialization lazy (built on first MappingFor(type) call rather
25          // than eagerly during ApplyConfiguration), DocumentMappingsWithSchema
26          // would otherwise enumerate an empty set when called pre-session.
27          // The descriptor snapshot is exactly that "pre-session" caller.
28          Options.Storage.BuildAllMappings();
29  
30          foreach (var mapping in Options.Storage.DocumentMappingsWithSchema.OrderBy(x => x.Alias))
31          {
32              usage.Documents.Add(BuildMappingDescriptor(mapping));
33          }
34  
35          // Flat OptionValues lifted up onto Properties bag — populated via the
36          // OptionsDescription auto-property reader through the base ctor, but
37          // we override several to coerce non-default shapes (enums-as-strings,
38          // Configured/Default masking, etc.).
39          ApplyFlatOptionValues(usage);
40  
41          // jasperfx#475 — advertise which document metadata Marten captures so
42          // store-aware consumers (CritterWatch) gate document-query facets by what is
43          // actually persisted. Version / last-modified / tenant / soft-delete are
44          // universal facets in Marten and keep the descriptor's default of true; the
45          // opt-in columns (correlation/causation/last-modified-by) are only queryable
46          // where some document mapping has enabled them.
47          var mappings = Options.Storage.DocumentMappingsWithSchema.ToList();
48          usage.DocumentMetadata = new DocumentMetadataCapabilities
49          {
50              StoreType = "Marten",
51              CorrelationId = mappings.Any(m => m.Metadata.CorrelationId.Enabled),
52              CausationId = mappings.Any(m => m.Metadata.CausationId.Enabled),
53              LastModifiedBy = mappings.Any(m => m.Metadata.LastModifiedBy.Enabled)
54          };
55  
56          return usage;
57      }

1  export function searchExplorer(rootValue: unknown, term: string): SearchMatch {
 2    const ancestors = new Set<unknown>()
 3    /**
 4     * Visits one original path with its current ancestors.
 5     * @param value - The entry value.
 6     * @param label - The entry label; absent for the synthetic root.
 7     * @param accessor - Whether reading the entry would invoke a getter.
 8     * @param depth - The current nesting depth.
 9     * @returns The entry's match metadata.
10     */
11    function visit(
12      value: unknown,
13      label?: string,
14      accessor = false,
15      depth = 0,
16    ): SearchMatch {
17      const labelMatch = label?.toLowerCase().includes(term) ?? false
18      const text = accessor ? undefined : primitiveText(value)
19      const valueMatch = text?.toLowerCase().includes(term) ?? false
20      const children = new Map<unknown, SearchMatch>()
21      const match: SearchMatch = {
22        label: labelMatch,
23        value: valueMatch,
24        hasMatch: labelMatch || valueMatch,
25        kind: accessor ? 'accessor' : text !== undefined ? 'value' : 'opaque',
26        children,
27      }
28      if (accessor || text !== undefined) return match
29      if (depth > 500) return match
30      if (ancestors.has(value)) {
31        match.kind = 'circular'
32        return match
33      }
34      const entries = searchEntries(value)
35      if (!entries) return match
36      match.kind = 'branch'
37      ancestors.add(value)
38      for (const entry of entries) {
39        const child = visit(entry.value, entry.label, entry.accessor, depth + 1)
40        children.set(entry.key, child)
41        match.hasMatch ||= child.hasMatch
42      }
43      ancestors.delete(value)
44      return match
45    }
46    return visit(rootValue)
47  }

1  export function getOption(
 2    optionsArgs: j.CallExpression['arguments'][number] | null,
 3    optionName: string
 4  ) {
 5    if (!optionsArgs || optionsArgs.type !== 'ObjectExpression') {
 6      return null;
 7    }
 8    const optionVals = optionsArgs.properties
 9      .map((p) =>
10        p.type === 'ObjectProperty' &&
11        p.key.type === 'Identifier' &&
12        p.key.name === optionName
13          ? p.value
14          : null
15      )
16      .filter((v) => v !== null);
17    const optionVal = optionVals[0];
18    return optionVal === undefined ||
19      optionVal.type === 'RestElement' ||
20      optionVal.type === 'SpreadElementPattern' ||
21      optionVal.type === 'PropertyPattern' ||
22      optionVal.type === 'ObjectPattern' ||
23      optionVal.type === 'ArrayPattern' ||
24      optionVal.type === 'AssignmentPattern' ||
25      optionVal.type === 'SpreadPropertyPattern' ||
26      optionVal.type === 'TSParameterProperty'
27      ? null
28      : optionVal;
29  }

1      internal static bool IsSimpleType(
 2          ITypeSymbol type,
 3          INamedTypeSymbol? formattableSymbol)
 4      {
 5          // A path value is emitted as UrlParameterFormatter.Format(value, provider, typeof(T)) - the same call the
 6          // reflection path uses - so any type the formatter can render round-trips identically. That is exactly the
 7          // set of IFormattable types (which is also what makes [Query(Format = ...)] and invariant culture work),
 8          // plus string and bool, which are scalars but not IFormattable. Collections, arrays and DTOs are excluded
 9          // and fall back to reflection. Matching on the resolved IFormattable symbol avoids per-parameter name-string
10          // allocations and automatically covers future BCL scalars.
11          var underlyingType = GetUnderlyingType(type);
12  
13          static ITypeSymbol GetUnderlyingType(ITypeSymbol type) =>
14              type is INamedTypeSymbol { OriginalDefinition.SpecialType: SpecialType.System_Nullable_T } nullable
15                  ? nullable.TypeArguments[0]
16                  : type;
17  
18          // The built-in value-type scalars occupy a contiguous SpecialType block - System_Boolean (bool, char,
19          // every integer width, decimal, float, double) through System_Double - so a range check covers them all
20          // in one comparison. string and DateTime sit just outside that block.
21          static bool IsScalarSpecialType(SpecialType specialType) =>
22              specialType is >= SpecialType.System_Boolean and <= SpecialType.System_Double
23              || specialType == SpecialType.System_String
24              || specialType == SpecialType.System_DateTime;
25  
26          // A null interfaceSymbol (System.IFormattable unresolved) simply matches nothing and falls back.
27          static bool ImplementsInterface(
28              ITypeSymbol type,
29              INamedTypeSymbol? interfaceSymbol)
30          {
31              foreach (var implemented in type.AllInterfaces)
32              {
33                  if (SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(implemented, interfaceSymbol))
34                  {
35                      return true;
36                  }
37              }
38  
39              return false;
40          }
41  
42          // Built-in scalars resolve from SpecialType alone (a jump table, no interface walk); everything else that
43          // renders to a URL scalar - enums, Guid, DateTimeOffset, DateOnly, TimeOnly, TimeSpan, BigInteger,
44          // Int128/UInt128, Half - implements IFormattable.
45          return IsScalarSpecialType(underlyingType.SpecialType)
46                 || ImplementsInterface(
47                     underlyingType,
48                     formattableSymbol)
49                 || IsUri(underlyingType)
50                 || IsCultureInfo(underlyingType);
51      }

28        fetchInfinite: () => context.fetchInfiniteQuery(queryKey, args[0]),

1      private computeDistinctCountExpression(columns: string[]): string {
 2          if (
 3              this.dataSource.driver.options.type === "cockroachdb" ||
 4              DriverUtils.isPostgresFamily(this.dataSource.driver)

 7              // https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.5/sql-select.html#SQL-DISTINCT
 8              return "COUNT(DISTINCT(" + columns.join(", ") + "))"
 9          }
10  
11          if (DriverUtils.isMySQLFamily(this.dataSource.driver)) {
12              // MySQL & MariaDB can pass multiple parameters to the `DISTINCT` language construct
13              // https://mariadb.com/kb/en/count-distinct/
14              return "COUNT(DISTINCT " + columns.join(", ") + ")"
15          }
16  
17          if (this.dataSource.driver.options.type === "mssql") {
18              // SQL Server has gotta be different from everyone else.  They don't support
19              // distinct counting multiple columns & they don't have the same operator
20              // characteristic for concatenating, so we gotta use the `CONCAT` function.
21              // However, If it's exactly 1 column we can omit the `CONCAT` for better performance.
22  
23              const columnsExpression = columns.join(", '|;|', ")
24  
25              if (columns.length === 1) {
26                  return `COUNT(DISTINCT(${columnsExpression}))`
27              }
28  
29              return `COUNT(DISTINCT(CONCAT(${columnsExpression})))`
30          }
31  
32          if (this.dataSource.driver.options.type === "spanner") {
33              // spanner also has gotta be different from everyone else.
34              // they do not support concatenation of different column types without casting them to string
35  
36              if (columns.length === 1) {
37                  return `COUNT(DISTINCT(${columns[0]}))`
38              }
39  
40              const columnsExpression = columns
41                  .map((column) => `CAST(${column} AS STRING)`)
42                  .join(", '|;|', ")
43              return `COUNT(DISTINCT(CONCAT(${columnsExpression})))`
44          }
45  
46          // If all else fails, fall back to a `COUNT` and `DISTINCT` across all the primary columns concatenated.
47          // Per the SQL spec, this is the canonical string concatenation mechanism which is most
48          // likely to work across servers implementing the SQL standard.
49  
50          // Please note, if there is only one primary column that the concatenation does not occur in this
51          // query and the query is a standard `COUNT DISTINCT` in that case.
52  
53          return `COUNT(DISTINCT(` + columns.join(" || '|;|' || ") + "))"
54      }

10              const alias = this.expressionMap.aliases.find(

1      private buildColumnSelectionExpression(
 2          aliasName: string,
 3          column: ColumnMetadata,
 4          includeHydrationTransform: boolean = true,

 9  
10          if (column.isVirtualProperty && column.query) {
11              selectionPath = `(${column.query(escapedAliasName)})`
12          }
13  
14          if (
15              DriverUtils.isSQLiteFamily(this.dataSource.driver) &&
16              includeHydrationTransform
17          ) {
18              selectionPath = (
19                  this.dataSource.driver as
20                      AbstractSqliteDriver | ReactNativeDriver
21              ).wrapWithJsonFunction(selectionPath, column, false)
22          }
23  
24          if (this.dataSource.driver.spatialTypes.indexOf(column.type) !== -1) {
25              if (
26                  (DriverUtils.isMySQLFamily(this.dataSource.driver) ||
27                      this.dataSource.driver.options.type === "aurora-mysql") &&
28                  includeHydrationTransform
29              ) {
30                  const useLegacy = (
31                      this.dataSource.driver as MysqlDriver | AuroraMysqlDriver
32                  ).options.legacySpatialSupport
33                  const asText = useLegacy ? "AsText" : "ST_AsText"
34                  selectionPath = `${asText}(${selectionPath})`
35              }
36  
37              if (
38                  DriverUtils.isPostgresFamily(this.dataSource.driver) &&
39                  includeHydrationTransform
40              )
41                  if (column.precision) {
42                      // cast to JSON to trigger parsing in the driver
43                      selectionPath = `ST_AsGeoJSON(${selectionPath}, ${column.precision})::json`
44                  } else {
45                      selectionPath = `ST_AsGeoJSON(${selectionPath})::json`
46                  }
47              if (this.dataSource.driver.options.type === "mssql")
48                  selectionPath = `${selectionPath}.ToString()`
49          }
50  
51          return selectionPath
52      }

 2          entities: Entity[]
 3          raw: any[]
 4      }): number | undefined {

 6              this.expressionMap.limit !== undefined &&
 7              this.expressionMap.limit !== null
 8          if (this.expressionMap.joinAttributes.length > 0 && hasLimit) {
 9              return undefined
10          }

13              this.expressionMap.take !== undefined &&
14              this.expressionMap.take !== null

17          const maxResults = hasLimit
18              ? this.expressionMap.limit

21                : undefined
22  
23          if (
24              maxResults !== undefined &&
25              entitiesAndRaw.entities.length === maxResults
26          ) {
27              // stop here when the result set contains the max number of rows; we need to execute a full count
28              return undefined
29          }
30  
31          const hasSkip =
32              this.expressionMap.skip !== undefined &&
33              this.expressionMap.skip !== null &&
34              this.expressionMap.skip > 0
35          const hasOffset =
36              this.expressionMap.offset !== undefined &&
37              this.expressionMap.offset !== null &&
38              this.expressionMap.offset > 0
39  
40          if (entitiesAndRaw.entities.length === 0 && (hasSkip || hasOffset)) {
41              // when skip or offset were used and no results found, we need to execute a full count
42              // (the given offset may have exceeded the actual number of rows)
43              return undefined
44          }
45  
46          // offset overrides skip when no join is defined
47          const previousResults: number = hasOffset
48              ? this.expressionMap.offset!
49              : hasSkip
50                ? this.expressionMap.skip!
51                : 0
52  
53          return entitiesAndRaw.entities.length + previousResults
54      }

 7          const inheritanceTree: any[] =

33                      ? mainTableOrAlias +
34                        "." +
35                        this.escape(metadata.discriminatorColumn.databaseName)

1  export function shorten(input: string, options: IShortenOptions = {}): string {
 2      const { segmentLength = 4, separator = "__", termLength = 2 } = options
 3  
 4      const segments = input.split(separator)
 5      const shortSegments = segments.reduce((acc: string[], val: string) => {
 6          // split the given segment into many terms based on an eventual camel cased name
 7          const segmentTerms = val
 8              .replaceAll(/([a-z\xE0-\xFF])([A-Z\xC0-\xDF])/g, "$1 $2")
 9              .replaceAll(/(_)([a-z])/g, " $2")
10              .split(" ")
11          // "OrderItemList" becomes "OrItLi", while "company" becomes "comp"
12          const length = segmentTerms.length > 1 ? termLength : segmentLength
13          const shortSegment = segmentTerms
14              .map((term) => term.slice(0, length))
15              .join("")
16  
17          acc.push(shortSegment)
18          return acc
19      }, [])
20  
21      return shortSegments.join(separator)
22  }

1  export function analyzeImportedModDifference(
 2    mod: any,
 3    rawId: string,
 4    moduleType: string | undefined,
 5    metadata?: SSRImportMetadata,
 6  ): void {
 7    // No normalization needed if the user already dynamic imports this module
 8    if (metadata?.isDynamicImport) return
 9  
10    // If the user named imports a specifier that can't be analyzed, error.
11    // If the module doesn't import anything explicitly, e.g. `import 'foo'` or
12    // `import * as foo from 'foo'`, we can skip.
13    if (metadata?.importedNames?.length) {
14      const missingBindings = metadata.importedNames.filter((s) => !(s in mod))
15      if (missingBindings.length) {
16        const lastBinding = missingBindings.at(-1)
17  
18        // For invalid named exports only, similar to how Node.js errors for top-level imports.
19        // But since we transform as dynamic imports, we need to emulate the error manually.
20        if (moduleType === 'module') {
21          throw new SyntaxError(
22            `[vite] The requested module '${rawId}' does not provide an export named '${lastBinding}'`,
23          )
24        } else {
25          // For non-ESM, named imports is done via static analysis with cjs-module-lexer in Node.js.
26          // Copied from Node.js
27          throw new SyntaxError(`\
28  [vite] Named export '${lastBinding}' not found. The requested module '${rawId}' is a CommonJS module, which may not support all module.exports as named exports.
29  CommonJS modules can always be imported via the default export, for example using:
30  
31  import pkg from '${rawId}';
32  const {${missingBindings.join(', ')}} = pkg;
33  `)
34        }
35      }
36    }
37  }

1  function removeInternal(s: MagicString, node: any): boolean {
 2    if (
 3      node.leadingComments &&
 4      node.leadingComments.some((c: any) => {
 5        return c.type === 'CommentBlock' && c.value.includes('@internal')
 6      })
 7    ) {
 8      // Examples:
 9      // function a(foo: string, /* @internal */ bar: number, baz: boolean)
10      //                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
11      // type Enum = Foo | /* @internal */ Bar | Baz
12      //                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
13      // strip trailing comma or pipe
14      const trailingRe = /\s*[,|]/y
15      trailingRe.lastIndex = node.end
16      const trailingStr = trailingRe.exec(s.original)?.[0] ?? ''
17      s.remove(node.leadingComments[0].start, node.end + trailingStr.length)
18      return true
19    }
20    return false
21  }

 2    raw: string,
 3    clean: string,
 4    i: number,
 5  ): Promise<WorkerType> {
 6    const commaIndex = clean.indexOf(',', i)
 7    if (commaIndex === -1) {
 8      return 'classic'
 9    }
10    const endIndex = findClosingParen(clean, i)
11  
12    // case: ') ... ,' mean no worker options params
13    if (commaIndex > endIndex) {
14      return 'classic'
15    }
16  
17    // need to find in comment code
18    let workerOptString = raw.substring(commaIndex + 1, endIndex)
19    const hasViteIgnore = hasViteIgnoreRE.test(workerOptString)
20    if (hasViteIgnore) {
21      return 'ignore'
22    }
23  
24    // need to find in no comment code
25    const cleanWorkerOptString = clean.substring(commaIndex + 1, endIndex)
26    const trimmedCleanWorkerOptString = cleanWorkerOptString.trim()
27    if (!trimmedCleanWorkerOptString.length) {
28      return 'classic'
29    }
30  
31    // strip trailing comma for evalValue
32    if (trimmedCleanWorkerOptString.endsWith(',')) {
33      workerOptString = workerOptString.slice(
34        0,
35        cleanWorkerOptString.lastIndexOf(','),
36      )
37    }
38  
39    const workerOpts = await parseWorkerOptions(workerOptString, commaIndex + 1)
40    if (
41      workerOpts.type &&
42      (workerOpts.type === 'module' || workerOpts.type === 'classic')
43    ) {
44      return workerOpts.type
45    }
46  
47    return 'classic'
48  }

 2    environment: Environment,
 3    file: string,
 4    id: string,

 6    /** Should be passed only in build */
 7    buildPluginContext: PluginContext | undefined,

 9  ): boolean {

13    if (buildPluginContext) {

19    // Don't inline SVG with fragments, as they are meant to be reused

27    } else {
28      limit = Number(assetsInlineLimit)
29    }
30    return content.length < limit && !isGitLfsPlaceholder(content)
31  }

25        attachment.contentType = contentType || undefined

28    }

1    async recordArtifact<Artifact extends TestArtifact>(

18

20      }
21  
22      if (Array.isArray(artifact.attachments)) {
23        await Promise.all(
24          artifact.attachments.map((attachment) => this.resolveTestAttachment(testCase, attachment)),
25        )
26      }
27  
28      // trace locations of browser tests need the browser server's source maps here,
29      // while node trace stacks are already mapped in the worker except for external modules
30      if (artifact.type === 'internal:browserTrace') {
31        const { entries } = artifact.data as BrowserTraceData
32        const project = testCase.project
33        const isBrowser = testCase.task.file.pool === 'browser'
34        for (const entry of entries) {
35          if (entry.stack && !entry.location) {
36            const [stack] = isBrowser
37              ? project.browser?.parseStacktrace(entry.stack, { firstOnly: true }) || []
38              : parseStacktrace(entry.stack, {
39                  firstOnly: true,
40                  getSourceMap: (file) => getExternalSourceMap(project, file),
41                })
42            if (stack) {

44            }
45          }
46        }
47      }
48  
49      testCase.task.artifacts.push(artifact)
50  
51      await this.vitest.report('onTestCaseArtifactRecord', testCase, artifact)
52  
53      return artifact
54    }

1  export function resolveOptimizerConfig(
 2    testOptions_: DepsOptimizationOptions | undefined,
 3    viteOptions: DepOptimizationOptions | undefined,
 4  ): DepOptimizationOptions {
 5    const testOptions = testOptions_ || {}
 6    let optimizeDeps: DepOptimizationOptions
 7    if (testOptions.enabled !== true) {
 8      testOptions.enabled ??= false
 9  
10      optimizeDeps = {
11        // experimental in Vite >2.9.2, entries remains to help with older versions
12        disabled: true,
13        entries: [],
14      }
15    } else {
16      const currentInclude = testOptions.include || viteOptions?.include || []
17      const exclude = [
18        'vitest',
19        // Ideally, we shouldn't optimize react in test mode, otherwise we need to optimize _every_ dependency that uses react.
20        'react',
21        'vue',
22        ...(testOptions.exclude || viteOptions?.exclude || []),
23      ]
24      const runtime = currentInclude.filter(
25        (n) => n.endsWith('jsx-dev-runtime') || n.endsWith('jsx-runtime'),
26      )
27      exclude.push(...runtime)
28  
29      const include = (testOptions.include || viteOptions?.include || []).filter(
30        (n: string) => !exclude.includes(n),
31      )
32  
33      optimizeDeps = {
34        ...viteOptions,
35        ...testOptions,
36        noDiscovery: true,
37        disabled: false,
38        entries: [],
39        exclude,
40        include,
41      }
42    }
43  
44    // `optimizeDeps.disabled` is deprecated since v5.1.0-beta.1
45    // https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/15184
46    if (optimizeDeps.disabled) {
47      optimizeDeps.noDiscovery = true
48      optimizeDeps.include = []
49    }
50    delete optimizeDeps.disabled
51  
52    return optimizeDeps
53  }

 2      sessionId: string,
 3      project: TestProject,
 4      pool: { reject: (error: Error) => void },

 8      const defer = createDefer<void>()
 9      let isConnected = false

11      const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
12        defer.reject(
13          new Error(
14            `Failed to connect to the browser session "${sessionId}" [${project.name}] within the timeout.`,

16        )

18  
19      const resolveIfReady = () => {
20        if (!isConnected || !isReady) {
21          return
22        }
23        defer.resolve()
24        clearTimeout(timeout)

31        concurrencyId: 0,

1  export function computeDurationBreakdown(input: DurationBreakdownInput): DurationBreakdown {
 2    const sums = {
 3      transform: 0,
 4      setup: 0,
 5      import: 0,
 6      tests: 0,
 7      environment: 0,
 8      worker: 0,
 9      typecheck: input.typecheckTime,
10    }
11    for (const file of input.files) {
12      // setup and collect wall times include the time the worker spent waiting
13      // for module transforms; report that wait as its own "transform" phase so
14      // every phase is a disjoint sum of per-worker time
15      const setupFetch = file.setupFetchDuration || 0
16      const collectFetch = file.collectFetchDuration || 0
17      sums.transform += setupFetch + collectFetch
18      sums.setup += Math.max((file.setupDuration || 0) - setupFetch, 0)
19      sums.import += Math.max((file.collectDuration || 0) - collectFetch, 0)
20      sums.tests += file.result?.duration || 0
21      sums.environment += file.environmentLoad || 0
22      sums.worker += file.prepareDuration || 0
23    }
24  
25    const entries = Object.entries(sums)
26    const total = entries.reduce((acc, [, time]) => acc + time, 0)
27    const phases = entries
28      .map(([name, time]) => ({
29        name,
30        time,
31        percent: total > 0 ? (time / total) * 100 : 0,
32      }))
33      .filter((phase) => phase.percent >= 0.5)
34      .sort((a, b) => b.time - a.time)
35  
36    return { total, phases }
37  }

 2      // happy-dom v3 introduced a breaking change to Window, but
 3      // provides GlobalWindow as a way to use previous behaviour
 4      const { Window, GlobalWindow } = await import('happy-dom')
 5      const win = new (GlobalWindow || Window)({
 6        ...happyDOM,
 7        console: console && global.console ? global.console : undefined,
 8        url: happyDOM.url || 'http://localhost:3000',
 9        settings: {
10          ...happyDOM.settings,
11          disableErrorCapturing: true,
12        },
13      })
14  
15      const { keys, originals } = populateGlobal(global, win, {
16        bindFunctions: true,
17        // jsdom doesn't support fetch API, but happy-dom does
18        additionalKeys: [
19          'Request',
20          'Response',
21          'MessagePort',
22          'fetch',
23          'Headers',
24          'AbortController',
25          'AbortSignal',
26          'URL',
27          'URLSearchParams',
28          'FormData',
29        ],
30      })
31  
32      return {
33        async teardown(global) {
34          await teardownWindow(win)
35          keys.forEach((key) => delete global[key])
36          originals.forEach((d, k) => Object.defineProperty(global, k, d))
37        },
38      }
39    }

 2    const raw = toRaw(array)

 5    if (isShallow(array)) return raw

13    ) as T[]
14  }

 6          }

 8          // A typed builder that was pointed at some other job through OfType would hand its job data to a
 9          // job that has no such properties. Nothing else can make these disagree, and a builder for IJob
10          // names no properties, so it has nothing to protect — which is also the only case where the type
11          // is a bare name, so this check never turns a name into an assembly probe.
12          if (typeof(TJob) != typeof(IJob) && _jobType.TryResolve(out var resolvedJobType)
13              && !typeof(TJob).IsAssignableFrom(resolvedJobType))
14          {
15              Throw.InvalidOperationException($"This builder configures a {typeof(TJob)}, but the job being built is a {resolvedJobType}.");
16          }
17  
18          // The two attribute-derived flags are left as they were stated - which may be "not stated at all".
19          // JobDetailImpl deduces an unstated one from the type when something asks for it and the type is
20          // at hand, so building a job out of a name that arrived over the wire neither loads nor probes for
21          // an assembly on the way. That deferral is what lets a client schedule a job whose type only the
22          // server has, and it is what keeps a hostile server from choosing an assembly name a client's
23          // runtime goes looking for.
24          return new JobDetailImpl(Key ?? new JobKey(Guid.NewGuid().ToString()),
25              _jobType,
26              _description,
27              _durability,
28              _shouldRecover,
29              jobDataMap.IsEmpty ? null : jobDataMap,
30              _concurrentExecutionDisallowed,
31              _persistJobDataAfterExecution);
32      }
